clue.text: Panic of feeder? What you'll see here in these short times of refreshment!

wordplay.reading: C OF FEE, split by spaces

parts.words: Panic of feeder? What you'll see here in these
parts.note: across the gaps in 'paniC OF FEEder' a hot drink can be read, broken up by the spaces between the words, which is what you see in these words

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm from someone doing the feeding, as though at a hectic tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is spread across three words of the clue, so it is what 'you'll see here', in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief pauses at work for a hot drink are the classic short refreshment interval.

clue.text: Store cold — that's a pain

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone complains that keeping things in cold storage hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden supply or hoard is a store of goods kept for later.

clue.text: Fawning female embarks on second year

parts.note: the latter of two things is the second one

explanation.surface: A woman begins her second year of something, perhaps at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawning behaviour is excessive praise and flattering attention, used here as a noun for that conduct.

clue.text: Sheep exercise from what we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: to exercise a right or tool is to use it

explanation.surface: Sheep taking exercise, as reported by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are called by this plural farm term.

clue.text: Afflicted in place of rest, bad, getting taken in hand

parts.note: a bed is where one rests
evil means bad
someone taken in hand is led or guided

explanation.surface: A troubled person in bed, behaving badly, has to be taken in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To be plagued or tormented by troubles is to be afflicted by them.

clue.text: Criticism when leader's not given guarantee

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for criticism is withheld

parts.note: censure is formal criticism

explanation.surface: A critic complains when the person in charge isn't offered any assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Book's ending on shelf, currently retained for learning

indicators.note: the pair of letters for the end of book plus shelf holds the word for currently within it
the final letter of the word Book is taken

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf
now means at the present time

explanation.surface: A library book ends up on a shelf, kept there for study.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning, as acquired information and understanding, is a synonym.

clue.text: Separating and losing emotional control?

definitions.meaning: splitting something into its parts, as a chemist decomposes a compound

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both dividing into components and collapsing emotionally.

clue.text: Nation needing a leader to make a surge before everyone else

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A country needs someone in charge to push it ahead of its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To surge forward past others is to sprint into the lead.

clue.text: Clean search

definitions.meaning: to scrub hard, as a pan

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both scrubbing hard and hunting thoroughly through a place.

clue.text: Sentries mope about — how long before call is answered?

definitions.text: how long before call is answered?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bored guards sulk around, perhaps waiting for an alarm to be answered.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval between an emergency call and its being dealt with is measured as this delay.

clue.text: Warnings — drinks may contain odd bits of rot

indicators.note: the word for drinks holds the picked letters inside it

parts.note: ales are beers, so drinks

clue.text: Perhaps maidens will conceal everything in loose clothing?

indicators.note: the word for maidens hides the word for everything inside it

parts.note: a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs, so maidens are examples of overs
all means everything

explanation.surface: Young women may hide everything in baggy garments.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is a set of six balls from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective garment worn over other clothes is roomy work wear.

clue.text: Fissures in foundation built on a large volume of water

indicators.note: the word for fissures sits inside the word for foundation

parts.note: a base is a foundation
rents are splits or tears

explanation.surface: Cracks in a building's foundations, which sits on a lot of water.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arctic sea north of Norway and Russia is a large body of water.

clue.text: One politician joining board wanting to include men that can be brought in

indicators.note: the combined pieces take the word for men within them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A politician joins a company board that needs more men on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods able to be imported can be brought into a country.

clue.text: Chemical bringing a measure of acidity into teashop unfortunately

indicators.note: the acidity measure goes inside the rearranged letters
unfortunately signals that the letters of teashop are in a bad, jumbled state

parts.note: pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: Something acidic gets into a café's products, unhappily.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of phosphoric acid is a chemical compound, common in fertilisers.

clue.text: The rejection of strange Eastern food — something starchy

parts.note: odd means strange

clue.text: Toes tilt awkwardly — in such a shoe?

indicators.note: awkwardly signals that the letters are placed clumsily, out of order

explanation.surface: Toes are tipped at an uncomfortable angle in a high-heeled shoe.

clue.text: Fool needs a message not to give up

definitions.text: a message not to give up

clue.text: About to join fast requiring not so much? Tharsh

less means not so much

explanation.surface: A dieter about to begin a fast that demands eating less.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is printed 'Tharsh', a typo for 'Harsh'.

clue.text: Girl is French, this female in book

her refers to a female

explanation.surface: A girl from France appears in a book.

explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne by the Jewish queen of the Bible.

clue.text: Facing work, poet is confused

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: confused signals that the letters of the poet phrase are muddled up

clue.text: Suffer defeat in court where accommodation for people is very limited

clue.text: Bargain? Something hard to be forged reportedly

parts.note: steel is a hard metal worked at a forge

clue.text: Adventurous womaniser's relationship

a tie or link between people

parts.note: neat means tidy and well-ordered

clue.text: Spanning a limited period that school-haters would welcome?

clue.text: Area shouldn't change completely

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are altered into a new order
